title: USB ambient light
brief: A USB powered ambient desk light with a button and individually addressable LEDs.
summary: An ESP32 controls a short 5 V LED strip through a level shifter. The wiring and power budget need checks against the exact strip, board and supply.

parts.name: ESP32 DevKit board
parts.detail: Choose an exact board and verify its USB power path and output GPIO.

parts.name: 5 V addressable LED strip, 30 LEDs
parts.detail: Choose a strip with documented current per LED and a 5 V data interface.

parts.name: 74AHCT125 level-shifter module
parts.detail: Translate 3.3 V data to 5 V. Confirm module pinout and common ground.

parts.name: 330 Ω resistor
parts.detail: Series data resistor near the LED input; verify against the strip maker guidance.

parts.name: 1000 µF capacitor, at least 6.3 V
parts.detail: Place across LED supply at strip input; observe polarity.

parts.name: Momentary pushbutton
parts.detail: Use a GPIO with an internal pull-up or add an external resistor.

parts.name: 5 V USB power supply, 3 A rated
parts.detail: Verify the worst-case LED current and cable rating before use.

parts.name: Diffuser and enclosure
parts.detail: Dimension and material choice depend on the final strip and heat test.

wires.note: Check chosen level shifter input pin.
Place resistor in series with the data line.
Connect at the marked strip input end.
Use a common ground with the controller.
Power via the ESP32 USB connector.

steps.title: Calculate power demand
steps.detail: Use the chosen strip datasheet to compute maximum current. Compare with supply, cable and connector ratings.

steps.title: Measure the fit
steps.detail: Measure strip width, bend radius, board size and connector clearance before making the enclosure.

steps.title: Build the data path
steps.detail: With power disconnected, wire GPIO to level shifter, series resistor and strip DIN. Tie grounds together.

steps.title: Connect power
steps.detail: Wire the strip directly to a suitable 5 V supply and the controller through its USB connector. Add the polarized input capacitor.

steps.title: Test at low brightness
steps.detail: Start with a few LEDs and a current limit. Confirm data direction and measure supply voltage at the far end.

steps.title: Check heat and strain relief
steps.detail: Run at expected brightness, inspect temperature and secure the cable entry.

tools: Calipers for the chosen strip and enclosure
assumptions: Exact LED strip, controller, level shifter and supply ratings need verification.
Maximum current and heat must be measured for the chosen operating brightness.
